newsitem.title: GERMANY: SKW Trostberg result seen improving.
newsitem.headline: SKW Trostberg result seen improving.

text.p: German specialty chemicals group SKW Trostberg AG posted slightly lower than expected nine-month results, but analysts agree business remains on track and in line for stronger future results.
"The SKW Trostberg story is still intact," said Kleinwort Benson analyst Lutz Grueten, even though nine-month numbers and some forecasts for the whole year were slightly below his own expectations.

The group, jumping ahead to become the world's largest construction chemicals company with this year's takeover of Master Builders Technologies from Swiss group Sandoz AG, said nine-month sales climbed four percent to 2.9 billion marks.
Operating profit, which the group declined to detail, was said to be at last year's high levels.
Bank Julius Baer analyst Martin Wirth said "Sales at SKW Trostberg were relatively weak, while earnings were around expectations, maybe a little higher than expected."
Analysts explained that weaker-than-expected sales may reflect sales lost through a divestment which several analysts had expected to become effective only in the fourth quarter.

Although the stock, which had become a market favourite since the group floated its shares last year, has taken a beating in recent days, analysts expected prices to recover soon, as investors take heart from SKW Trostberg's plan to present steady, strong growth.

The company said the recent drop in share prices was due to earlier, unrealistic results expectations as well as fund managers freeing up room to take in the newly-launched Deutsche Telekom AG shares.
The shares recovered ground on Wednesday, closing bourse trade up 1.49 marks at 42.89 marks.
Looking ahead, SKW Trostberg expects 1997 earnings to outpace sales, even though it said the 1.3 billion Swiss franc price tag for MBT will weigh on 1997 net profit.
In the longer run, however, analysts welcomed the group's aggressive acquisitions policy which has brought in both MBT and Systems Bio-Industries, purchased from French group Sanofi SA two years ago.
While the MBT cost was high, swelling SKW Trostberg's debt to two billion marks, the market was relieved by the group's plans to finance the takeover with bank loans rather than a capital rise.

But analysts also said a capital increase may again become an option by the middle of next year. SKW Trostberg, at its flotation, said it wanted to stock up its war chest to be ready to jump when an interesting opportunity presented itself.

At the sidelines of a news conference, officials again said a capital rise was not being considered to finance MBT but should not be ruled out altogether as the group is still eager to participate in the general consolidation going on in the industry at the moment.
But the group's earnings per share estimates, seen to be around 2.20 marks this year and higher next year, created some confusion among analysts.
Christiane Dienhart, analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, said she was maintaining her "neutral" forecast for SKW Trostberg until the company clarified its statements on its EPS outlook.

"We are keeping our EPS outlook for 1996 at 2.35 marks, and have revised our EPS forecast for 1997 downwards to 2.85 marks from 2.95 marks. We need to speak to the management before we can decide what to do with the rating," said Dienhart.
